headline: Germany passes CRA implementation law; CBAM deduction rules take shape

summary.text: The Bundesrat approved Germany's Cyber Resilience Act implementation law, so machine and device makers should now plan for CRA security, reporting and conformity obligations.
CBAM rules on deducting carbon prices paid in third countries are clarifying, and the EU accepting India's CCTS may lower certificate costs and change documentation for importers.
A possible CBAM extension to more aluminium products and a UK-EU accord on free allocation could shift carbon cost exposure for metal importers and exporters.
Rockwell Automation plans to acquire AGILOX, and ABB's palletizing template reportedly cuts cobot deployment time by up to 80% (vendor-reported), making automation easier to enter.
Practical references are available: an Atlas Copco cobot with a 10.5-month payback, a Varta Microbattery digital twin, and a Chemnitz robotics and AI workshop for the Mittelstand.

actions.text: Product managers and TMG consultants should inventory connected products and start a CRA gap analysis covering security requirements, vulnerability reporting and conformity assessment against the new German implementation law.
Purchasing and customs teams importing CBAM-covered goods, especially aluminium or goods from India, should check eligibility and documentation for deducting third-country carbon prices.
Production heads considering automation should use the 10.5-month cobot payback as a benchmark and ask ABB or integrators about palletizing templates for a quote.
